{{Short description|Physicist}}
'''Lee Wendel Casperson''' (born 1944) is an American physicist and engineer.

Casperson earned his bachelor of science degree from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1966. He then pursued a master of science and doctorate at the [[California Institute of Technology]], graduating in 1971.<ref name="uncchar">{{cite news |title=Dr. Lee Casperson, Ph.D |url=https://ece.charlotte.edu/directory/dr-lee-casperson-phd |access-date=7 May 2022}}</ref> Casperson subsequently taught at the [[Portland State University]].<ref name="psu">{{cite news |title=Emeritus faculty |url=https://www.pdx.edu/electrical-computer-engineering/faculty#EmeritusFaculty |access-date=7 May 2022 |publisher=Portland State University}}</ref> While at Portland, he was elected a fellow of the IEEE,<ref name="psu"/> as well as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="apsfellow">{{cite news |title=APS fellow archive |url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=C&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=7 May 2022 |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref> He later joined the faculty of the [[University of North Carolina at Charlotte]].<ref name="uncchar"/>
